page: Microsoft Azure EC64ads_cc_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor. It features 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The server is equipped with 512 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. It includes 2458 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

In benchmark testing, this instance demonstrates strong multi-core and memory performance. The Passmark memory score ranks in the top 10%, supported by a cached read-only small-block memory bandwidth of 4162.65 GB/sec. Multi-core execution is highly efficient, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores all placing in the top 25%. It also excels in database operations, achieving 62.79 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and strong Passmark database scores. However, uncached large-block memory bandwidth and single-core tasks, such as Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression, perform in the average range. Large-model LLM text generation is a notable bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25% due to the lack of hardware GPU acceleration.

Given its high memory density and integrated 2.4 TB local storage, the EC64ads_cc_v5 offers a resource-dense profile for workloads requiring substantial memory capacity without the overhead of external storage attachments. This makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive applications, relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and multi-threaded software compilation. It is less optimal for workloads requiring specialized matrix math acceleration or large-scale LLM inference.
